# Plan, run and report survey research

Design your questionnaire, plan your analysis and prepare an APA 7
report. Work visually in SurveyStudio or use R.

For people conducting, supervising, reviewing or planning survey
research.

[Explore templates](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates.md) [Get
started](https://surveyframe.org/articles/start.md)

SurveyStudio opens through R. The [setup
guide](https://surveyframe.org/articles/start.md) explains installing
the required software and opening your first study.

[![CRAN
status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/surveyframe)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=surveyframe)
[![CRAN
downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/surveyframe)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=surveyframe)
[![License:
MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

## Conducting a survey for your studies?

Plan your research, create your questionnaire, analyse responses and
prepare your report. [Guidance for survey
students](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/for-students.md)

## Supervising students conducting survey research?

Review each student’s analysis plan, compare it with the completed
report and follow recorded amendments and their reasons. [Guidance for
supervisors](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/for-supervisors.md)

## Reviewing a survey study as an ethics committee?

Examine the proposed study documentation, then review the completed
study and its recorded changes. [Guidance for ethics
committees](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/for-ethics-committees.md)

## Planning survey research for an NGO or research organisation?

Prepare a pre-analysis plan and keep the questionnaire, analysis
decisions and reporting connected. [Guidance for NGOs and research
organisations](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/for-research-organisations.md)

## Keep your questionnaire and analysis plan connected

Save your questions, scoring rules, analysis plan and references in a
portable `.sframe` file. Collect responses using your chosen setup,
check their quality and prepare a report that presents the planned
analyses alongside the results and your interpretation.

Record later changes with their reasons so readers can follow the
study’s development.

**Plan your study before collecting responses.** Record your research
questions, hypotheses and analysis choices alongside the questionnaire.
[How to write the analysis
plan](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/analysis-plan.md).

**Move from responses to a research report.** Check the collected
responses, run the planned analyses and prepare APA 7 tables, figures
and references for supported methods. [See the report
stage](https://surveyframe.org/articles/run-a-study-in-surveystudio.html#report).

**Keep a record of your research design.** Preserve the questionnaire
version, sources and disclosed amendments with the design file. [Verify
a `.sframe` file](https://surveyframe.org/verify/) to check that it
matches the hash recorded when it was saved.

For example, start with the [course evaluation
survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/course-evaluation-survey.md),
plan how you will summarise the ratings, collect responses and prepare a
report for the teaching team. It is an example to adapt to your own
course and questions.

## Start from a template

Each template holds a questionnaire and an example analysis plan to
adapt to your own study.

**Psychology and measurement.** [Likert scale
questionnaire](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/likert-scale-questionnaire.md),
[Measurement model questionnaire (CFA and
SEM)](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/measurement-model-questionnaire.md).

**Education.** [Course evaluation
survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/course-evaluation-survey.md),
[Training evaluation before and
after](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/training-evaluation-before-and-after.md).

**Business.** [Customer satisfaction
survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/customer-satisfaction-survey.md),
[Employee engagement
survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/employee-engagement-survey.md),
[Supplier and venue selection (decision
making)](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/supplier-and-venue-selection.md).

**Events and tourism.** [Open-ended feedback
survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/open-ended-feedback-survey.md).

**Research methods.** [Pilot survey with a small
sample](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/pilot-survey-small-sample.md),
[Preparing a survey study for
preregistration](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/pre-registered-survey-sealed-and-amended.md).

[All questionnaire
templates](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates.md)

## How a study runs

1.  **Design** the questionnaire and write the analysis plan, with
    hypotheses and decision rules, before collecting responses.
2.  **Collect** responses with a survey web page, stored where you
    choose, such as a Google Sheet you own.
3.  **Check** responses for failed attention checks, speeding, identical
    answers across a scale and missing answers.
4.  **Analyse** the responses with the plan as written. A later change
    is recorded as an amendment with its reason.
5.  **Report** in APA 7, as HTML, Word, PDF or OpenDocument.

[Run a study in
SurveyStudio](https://surveyframe.org/articles/run-a-study-in-surveystudio.md)
shows each stage by point and click, and [Run a study in
R](https://surveyframe.org/articles/run-a-study-in-r.md) shows the same
stages in R.

Already use R? Open a first study from the Console

``` r

install.packages("surveyframe")
library(surveyframe)
d <- sframe_demo("first_survey")
```

Then read the [R reference](https://surveyframe.org/reference/index.md),
the [worked
examples](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn-by-example.md) and the
[changelog](https://surveyframe.org/news/index.md).

# Articles

## Questionnaire templates

10 example questionnaires, each with an analysis plan to adapt and
screenshots of the study in SurveyStudio, grouped by field.

- [Questionnaire
  templates](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates.md):

  10 example questionnaires, each with an analysis plan to adapt, in
  psychology, education, business, events and tourism, and research
  methods.

- [Course evaluation
  survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/course-evaluation-survey.md):

  A course evaluation in which students rate each part of a course on 1
  grid, compared between students who took it in person and online.
  surveyframe gives you the questionnaire, the analysis plan and a
  report for the teaching team.

- [Customer satisfaction
  survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/customer-satisfaction-survey.md):

  A customer study of return intention: whether customers who use a
  service more come back, and how that use relates to their satisfaction
  and the offer they prefer. surveyframe gives you the questionnaire, a
  plan with logistic regressions declared in advance, and the report.

- [Employee engagement
  survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/employee-engagement-survey.md):

  An engagement survey of 8 items written to measure 2 dimensions, how
  work is organised and the content of the work, with a check that
  employees’ answers support 2 scores. surveyframe gives you the
  questionnaire, the analysis plan and the report.

- [Likert scale
  questionnaire](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/likert-scale-questionnaire.md):

  A short questionnaire that measures 1 idea with a 4-item Likert scale,
  including a reverse-worded item, and checks that the scale holds
  together before its score is used. surveyframe gives you the
  questionnaire, a pre-analysis plan to submit with your proposal, and
  an APA 7 report.

- [Measurement model questionnaire (CFA and
  SEM)](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/measurement-model-questionnaire.md):

  A study exploring a proposed relationship between content quality,
  satisfaction and the intention to return. Specify the measurement and
  structural model, then generate syntax for lavaan or seminr.
  surveyframe gives you the questionnaire, the model syntax and the
  report.

- [Open-ended feedback
  survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/open-ended-feedback-survey.md):

  A feedback survey of what worked and what to change, analysed as text:
  frequent words and phrases, words in context, sentiment and topics.
  surveyframe gives you the questionnaire, the analysis plan and the
  report.

- [Pilot survey with a small
  sample](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/pilot-survey-small-sample.md):

  A pilot with 18 participants that answers the main study’s questions
  with methods suited to a small sample: a rank-based comparison, an
  exact test and a penalised logistic regression. surveyframe gives you
  the questionnaire, the pre-analysis plan and the report.

- [Preparing a survey study for
  preregistration](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/pre-registered-survey-sealed-and-amended.md):

  A survey study whose instrument and analysis plan are saved with a
  hash before data collection, with any later change recorded as a
  disclosed amendment. surveyframe writes a pre-analysis plan for you to
  complete and register on OSF or Zenodo, and a report that names the
  instrument it analysed.

- [Supplier and venue selection (decision
  making)](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/supplier-and-venue-selection.md):

  Compare candidate suppliers or venues using the criteria your
  committee values. Record the criteria and the judgements, then review
  the rankings your selected methods produce. surveyframe gives you the
  questionnaire, the analysis plan and the report.

- [Training evaluation before and
  after](https://surveyframe.org/articles/templates/training-evaluation-before-and-after.md):

  Compare the same participants’ confidence, and their willingness to
  recommend a workshop, before and after the training. Plan the paired
  comparisons before collecting responses. surveyframe gives you the
  questionnaire, the plan and the report.

## How-to guides

Complete tasks, from setting up a questionnaire to analysing responses
and recording the study, each in SurveyStudio and in R.

- [How-to guides](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides.md):

  Follow a complete task, from setting up a questionnaire to analysing
  responses and documenting your study, in SurveyStudio and in R.

- [How to add a welcome page, a logo and a colour to a
  survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/add-a-welcome-page-a-logo-and-a-colour-to-a-survey.md):

  Personalise a survey with a welcome page, your organisation’s logo and
  a theme colour.

- [How to analyse a grid of rating
  questions](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/analyse-a-grid-of-rating-questions.md):

  Summarise the ratings for each row of a grid question and compare them
  between groups.

- [How to analyse a survey with fewer than 30
  respondents](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/analyse-a-survey-with-fewer-than-30-respondents.md):

  Plan and review an analysis for a survey with a small sample, such as
  a pilot.

- [How to analyse choose-any and ranking
  questions](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/analyse-choose-any-and-ranking-questions.md):

  Summarise questions where respondents tick any options or put options
  in order.

- [How to analyse open-ended
  answers](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/analyse-open-ended-answers.md):

  Explore what respondents wrote in open-ended answers: the frequent
  words, how a word is used, the topics and the tone.

- [How to ask questions only of those they apply
  to](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/ask-questions-only-of-those-they-apply-to.md):

  Show a question only to respondents whose earlier answer makes it
  apply to them.

- [How to change a questionnaire mid-study, on the
  record](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/change-a-questionnaire-mid-study-on-the-record.md):

  Change a questionnaire during a study and record the change with its
  reason.

- [How to check whether a Likert scale holds
  together](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/check-whether-a-likert-scale-holds-together.md):

  Check whether the items of a Likert scale measure 1 thing well enough
  to combine into a score.

- [How to check whether your items measure the factors you
  assumed](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/check-whether-your-items-measure-the-factors-you-assumed.md):

  Explore whether your items group into the factors you expected.

- [How to choose between options on multiple
  criteria](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/choose-between-options-on-multiple-criteria.md):

  Rank decision options by criteria weighted by the people you asked.

- [How to cite the sources of a scale and a
  method](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/cite-the-sources-of-a-scale-and-a-method.md):

  Keep the sources of your scale and your methods with the study, and
  cite them in the report.

- [How to combine 1 question at a time with skip
  logic](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/combine-1-question-at-a-time-with-skip-logic.md):

  Combine a survey shown 1 question at a time with questions that depend
  on earlier answers.

- [How to compare 2 groups on a survey
  outcome](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/compare-2-groups-on-a-survey-outcome.md):

  Compare a numeric outcome between 2 independent groups of respondents.

- [How to compare 3 or more groups, with a
  covariate](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/compare-3-or-more-groups-with-a-covariate.md):

  Compare an outcome across 3 or more groups, add a second factor, and
  adjust for a covariate.

- [How to compare 3 or more measurements of the same
  people](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/compare-3-or-more-measurements-of-the-same-people.md):

  Compare 3 or more measurements taken from the same respondents.

- [How to compare the same people before and
  after](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/compare-the-same-people-before-and-after.md):

  Compare answers from the same respondents before and after an
  activity.

- [How to find what goes with an outcome, and how much it
  explains](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/find-what-goes-with-an-outcome-and-how-much-it-explains.md):

  Find which measures go together with an outcome, and how much of it
  they explain together.

- [How to predict a yes or no, an ordered rating or a
  choice](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/predict-a-yes-or-no-an-ordered-rating-or-a-choice.md):

  Choose and run a model for an outcome that is a yes or no, an ordered
  rating or a choice between categories.

- [How to prove a questionnaire file is the one you
  planned](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/prove-a-questionnaire-file-is-the-one-you-planned.md):

  Check that a questionnaire file matches the hash recorded when it was
  saved.

- [How to run a complete survey, from questionnaire to report, in
  R](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/run-a-complete-survey-from-questionnaire-to-report-in-r.md):

  Run a whole survey study in R: write the questionnaire and its plan,
  collect responses, check them, analyse them as planned and write the
  report.

- [How to show a survey 1 question at a
  time](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/show-a-survey-1-question-at-a-time.md):

  Present your survey 1 question at a time, with a progress bar.

- [How to test a measurement and structural
  model](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/test-a-measurement-and-structural-model.md):

  Declare the measurement and structural model for your constructs, take
  its syntax to lavaan or seminr to fit it, and test mediation and
  moderation.

- [How to test mediation and
  moderation](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/test-mediation-and-moderation.md):

  Test whether a variable carries an effect (mediation) or changes its
  strength (moderation).

- [How to test whether 2 categorical answers are
  associated](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/test-whether-2-categorical-answers-are-associated.md):

  Test whether 2 categorical answers are associated.

- [How to weight a survey sample to its
  population](https://surveyframe.org/articles/guides/weight-a-survey-sample-to-its-population.md):

  Apply survey weights so your summaries describe the population the
  sample was drawn from.

## Documentation

How to set up each question type and each analysis method, with
screenshots of SurveyStudio.

- [Documentation: how to set up
  surveyframe](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs.md):

  How to set up each question type and analysis in surveyframe, step by
  step, with annotated SurveyStudio screenshots.

- [Test an association between
  categories](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/associations.md):

  These methods test whether 2 categorical answers go together.

- [Choose a
  method](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/choose-a-method.md):

  From the research question to the analysis method a plan stores, in 4
  charts.

- [Measure how answers go
  together](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/correlations.md):

  These methods measure how strongly 2 numeric or ordered answers move
  together, and whether that holds with a third held constant.

- [Add a criteria weighting
  question](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/criteria-weights.md):

  Add a question, choose Criteria weight, and list the criteria to
  divide 100 points across.

- [Add a date
  question](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/date.md):

  Add a question and choose Date. The respondent picks it from a
  calendar.

- [Choose between
  options](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/decisions.md):

  These methods weigh each criterion and rank the options.

- [Describe the answers and their
  quality](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/describing-data.md):

  These methods describe who answered what, how complete the answers
  are, and which responses the quality checks flag.

- [Check structure and write model
  syntax](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/factor-models.md):

  These methods check whether items measure the factors assumed, write
  the lavaan or seminr syntax for a declared model, and estimate
  mediation and moderation.

- [Add a grid of rating
  questions](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/grid.md):

  Add a question, choose Matrix, list the rows, and pick the scale every
  row is rated on.

- [Compare
  groups](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/group-comparisons.md):

  These methods test whether an outcome differs between 2 or more groups
  of respondents.

- [Add a Likert question to a
  scale](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/likert.md):

  Add a question, choose Likert, and choose the choice set that holds
  its answer options, such as Strongly disagree to Strongly agree.

- [Add an open-ended
  question](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/long-text.md):

  Add a question and choose Long text for a paragraph.

- [Add a choose-any
  question](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/multiple-choice.md):

  Add a question, choose Multiple choice, and give the options the
  respondent may tick.

- [Add a number
  question](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/numeric.md):

  Add a question, choose Numeric, and set the range the answer may take.

- [Add pairwise
  comparisons](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/pairwise-comparison.md):

  Choose the task first. To find which criteria matter most (AHP, ANP),
  use Saaty’s importance scale. To find how criteria influence each
  other (DEMATEL), use the influence scale. Then add a question, choose
  Pairwise comparison and list the criteria.

- [Add a ranking
  question](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/ranking.md):

  Add a question, choose Ranking, and give the options to put in order.

- [Predict an
  outcome](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/regression.md):

  These methods estimate how much predictors explain a numeric outcome,
  or how they change the odds of a yes, an ordered rating or a choice.

- [Compare the same people over
  time](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/repeated-measures.md):

  These methods test whether answers change between 2 or more
  measurements of the same respondents.

- [Score a scale and check its
  reliability](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/scales-reliability.md):

  These methods give a scale’s score and test whether its items hold
  together.

- [Add a short text
  question](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/short-text.md):

  Add a question and choose Short text for a word or a line.

- [Add a single-choice
  question](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/single-choice.md):

  Add a question, choose Single choice, and give the options the
  respondent picks 1 from.

- [Add a slider
  rating](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/slider.md):

  Add a question, choose Slider, and set its range and step.

- [Add a star
  rating](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/question-types/star-rating.md):

  Add a question and choose Rating for a row of stars.

- [Analyse open
  answers](https://surveyframe.org/articles/docs/methods/text-analysis.md):

  These methods find the words, phrases, contexts, tones and topics in
  open answers.

## Get started and learn

Install surveyframe and open a study in SurveyStudio, guidance for each
audience, the frequently asked questions, comparisons with other tools,
and how to cite surveyframe.

- [Get started with
  surveyframe](https://surveyframe.org/articles/start.md):

  Install R, RStudio and surveyframe, open an example study in
  SurveyStudio, then turn a downloaded template into your own study, by
  point and click in SurveyStudio.

- [Cite surveyframe](https://surveyframe.org/articles/cite.md):

  How to cite surveyframe in a thesis or paper: the APA 7 reference, the
  BibTeX entry and the DOI.

- [Plan first, analyse second: the analysis plan in
  surveyframe](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/analysis-plan.md):

  How to plan your analysis before collecting responses: for each
  research question, what you expect to find, the measurements you will
  use and how you will analyse them.

- [Choosing a survey tool for
  research](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/choosing-a-survey-tool.md):

  What to look for in a survey tool for research: the analysis plan,
  preregistration, reporting, data ownership and reproducibility, and
  where surveyframe fits.

- [Frequently asked
  questions](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/faq.md):

  Answers about surveyframe: using it for a thesis, preregistering on
  OSF, planning first and creative thinking, working by point and click
  in SurveyStudio, collecting answers, and checking a questionnaire
  file.

- [Reviewing survey studies for an ethics
  committee](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/for-ethics-committees.md):

  Guidance for ethics committees: review the proposed questionnaire and
  study plan before collection, identify the submitted instrument
  version, then review the completed report and its recorded changes.

- [Survey research for NGOs and research
  organisations](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/for-research-organisations.md):

  Guidance for NGOs and research organisations: prepare a pre-analysis
  plan, connect it to the questionnaire, document analysis decisions and
  amendments, and report the completed study to stakeholders.

- [Survey research for your
  studies](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/for-students.md):

  Guidance for students conducting a survey study: choose and adapt an
  example, write the questionnaire and analysis plan, collect and check
  responses, and produce the study report.

- [Supervising survey
  research](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/for-supervisors.md):

  Guidance for supervisors: review a student’s questionnaire and
  analysis plan, keep the agreed version, compare the completed report
  with the plan, and inspect recorded amendments and their reasons.

- [Choosing questions for your
  survey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/question-types.md):

  Choose a question type to match the information you need, from
  agreement ratings and dates to written feedback and ranked options,
  with the analyses each type suits.

- [Register your analysis plan on
  OSF](https://surveyframe.org/articles/learn/register-on-osf.md):

  How to preregister a surveyframe study on the Open Science Framework:
  write the pre-analysis plan, complete the remaining fields, and upload
  it with the .sframe file.

- [surveyframe and Google
  Forms](https://surveyframe.org/articles/compare/google-forms.md):

  How surveyframe relates to Google Forms: what each does, what
  surveyframe adds for research, and how to analyse Google Forms
  responses with surveyframe.

- [surveyframe and
  LimeSurvey](https://surveyframe.org/articles/compare/limesurvey.md):

  How surveyframe relates to LimeSurvey: what each does, what
  surveyframe adds for research, and how to analyse LimeSurvey responses
  with surveyframe.

- [surveyframe and
  Qualtrics](https://surveyframe.org/articles/compare/qualtrics.md):

  How surveyframe relates to Qualtrics: what each does, what surveyframe
  adds for research, and how to analyse Qualtrics responses with
  surveyframe.

- [surveyframe and
  surveydown](https://surveyframe.org/articles/compare/surveydown.md):

  How surveyframe relates to surveydown: what each does, what
  surveyframe adds for research, and how to analyse surveydown responses
  with surveyframe.

## Survey research workflow

Read these in order. Start with the worked example, then build the
instrument, analyse responses, check reliability and validity, generate
model syntax, and finish with the visual tools.

- [Survey design and live results: a tourism services
  example](https://surveyframe.org/articles/surveyframe.md):
- [Building a survey instrument: questions, plan, and
  model](https://surveyframe.org/articles/building-survey-instrument.md):
- [Deploying a survey and collecting responses on free
  hosting](https://surveyframe.org/articles/deploying-and-collecting.md):
- [Analysing survey responses: running the
  plan](https://surveyframe.org/articles/analysing-survey-responses.md):
- [Scale reliability and
  validity](https://surveyframe.org/articles/scale-reliability-validity.md):
- [EFA, CFA, CB-SEM, and PLS-SEM syntax
  generation](https://surveyframe.org/articles/efa-cfa-sem-pls-syntax.md):
- [The visual workflow: SurveyBuilder, SurveyStudio, and the
  dashboard](https://surveyframe.org/articles/surveybuilder-gui-overview.md):

## Specialised analyses

Read these when a study calls for them. Small-sample inference covers
studies below the n = 30 threshold, multi-criteria decision analysis
covers ranking alternatives against criteria that compete, and text
analysis covers open-ended survey responses.

- [Small-sample
  inference](https://surveyframe.org/articles/small-sample.md):
- [Multi-criteria decision
  analysis](https://surveyframe.org/articles/mcdm-analysis.md):
- [Text and open-ended response
  analysis](https://surveyframe.org/articles/text-analysis.md):

# R reference

## Start here

SurveyStudio opens an instrument and takes it through every stage below,
by point and click. ?surveyframe is the map of the package, and
sframe_demo(“first_survey”) is a whole survey to start from.

- [`surveyframe`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/surveyframe-package.md)
  [`surveyframe-package`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/surveyframe-package.md)
  : surveyframe: Design, Plan, Seal and Report Questionnaire Studies
- [`launch_studio()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/launch_studio.md)
  : Launch the SurveyStudio interface

## Design

Make the instrument: its questions, choice sets, scales, branching and
attention checks, saved as a portable .sframe file. In SurveyBuilder:
the Build mode. In code:
[`sframe_instrument()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_instrument.md)
and the makers listed here, then
[`write_sframe()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/write_sframe.md).

- [`launch_builder()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/launch_builder.md)
  : Launch the surveyframe visual survey builder
- [`sframe_instrument()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_instrument.md)
  : Create a survey instrument object
- [`sframe_get_study()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_get_study.md)
  : The study an instrument serves
- [`sframe_sampling_methods()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_sampling_methods.md)
  : Sampling methods a study can declare
- [`sframe_item()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_item.md) :
  Define a survey item
- [`sframe_choice_set()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_choice_set.md)
  : Define a reusable choice set
- [`sframe_scale()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_scale.md)
  : Define a scored scale
- [`sframe_branch()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_branch.md)
  : Define a branching rule
- [`sframe_attention_check()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_attention_check.md)
  : Define a design-time survey check
- [`sframe_conjoint_design()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_conjoint_design.md)
  : Declare a choice-experiment (conjoint) design
- [`write_sframe()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/write_sframe.md)
  : Write an instrument to a .sframe file
- [`read_sframe()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/read_sframe.md) :
  Read an instrument from a .sframe file
- [`validate_sframe()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/validate_sframe.md)
  : Validate an instrument object
- [`sframe_validation`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_validation.md)
  : Report on a validation result
- [`as_sframe()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as_sframe.md) :
  Coerce to an instrument

## Plan

Declare the analysis before the data arrive, so the report shows what
was planned and what was run. In SurveyBuilder: the Plan mode. In
SurveyStudio: Plan, or the Analyse screen. In code:
`sframe_plan(x) <- plan`.

- [`sframe_plan()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plan.md) :
  Get the pre-declared analysis plan
- [`` `sframe_plan<-`() ``](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plan-set.md)
  : Set the pre-declared analysis plan
- [`sframe_sample_size_plan()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_sample_size_plan.md)
  : Plan the sample size for an analysis

## Preview

See the survey as a respondent meets it, with nothing collected. In
SurveyStudio: the Preview screen. In code:
[`preview_survey()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/preview_survey.md).

- [`preview_survey()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/preview_survey.md)
  : Preview a survey as a respondent sees it
- [`run_survey()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/run_survey.md) :
  Render a survey from an instrument object

## Collect

Send the survey out: a standalone HTML page, optionally saving answers
to a Google Sheet, or a Shiny module inside your own app. In
SurveyBuilder: Export survey, with the Google Sheets settings. In code:
[`export_survey()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/export_survey.md).

- [`export_survey()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/export_survey.md)
  : Export a self-contained static HTML survey
- [`export_google_sheet()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/export_google_sheet.md)
  : Export a survey instrument to Google Sheets collection format
- [`sframe_survey_ui()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_survey_ui.md)
  : Shiny module UI for an embedded survey
- [`sframe_survey_server()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_survey_server.md)
  : Shiny module server for an embedded survey

## Responses

Read the answers back against the instrument, check their quality, and
export them with labels for other software. In SurveyStudio: the
Responses and Quality screens. In code:
[`read_responses()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/read_responses.md).

- [`read_responses()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/read_responses.md)
  : Read and validate survey responses
- [`read_sheet_responses()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/read_sheet_responses.md)
  : Read survey responses from a Google Sheet
- [`export_responses()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/export_responses.md)
  : Write responses to SPSS or Stata with the labels attached
- [`sframe_quality_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_quality_results.md)
  : Generate a data quality report for survey responses
- [`sframe_missing_data_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_missing_data_results.md)
  : Missing-data report
- [`sframe_outlier_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_outlier_results.md)
  : Flag univariate and multivariate outliers

## Analyse

Score the scales and run the plan, block by block. In SurveyStudio: the
Explore, Reliability and Analyse screens. In code:
[`run_analysis_plan()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/run_analysis_plan.md).

- [`run_analysis_plan()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/run_analysis_plan.md)
  : Run a pre-planned analysis from an instrument's analysis plan
- [`score_scales()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/score_scales.md)
  : Score defined scales from survey responses
- [`sframe_descriptives_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_descriptives_results.md)
  : Descriptive statistics report
- [`sframe_reliability_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_reliability_results.md)
  : Estimate scale reliability from item responses
- [`sframe_item_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_item_results.md)
  : Generate item-level diagnostics
- [`sframe_efa_readiness_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_efa_readiness_results.md)
  : Check whether scale items are ready for exploratory factor analysis
- [`sframe_efa_solution()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_efa_solution.md)
  : Estimate an exploratory factor solution
- [`sframe_validity_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_validity_results.md)
  : Validity report for construct models
- [`sframe_assumption_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_assumption_results.md)
  : Assumption-check report
- [`sframe_posthoc_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_posthoc_results.md)
  : Post-hoc and pairwise comparison report

## Report

Write up what was run: an HTML, PDF, Word or OpenDocument report or its
Quarto source, a codebook, the figures, and the R code behind each
result, and
[`sframe_show()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_show.md) to
open a written file. In SurveyStudio: the Report screen. In code:
[`render_report()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/render_report.md).

- [`render_report()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/render_report.md)
  : Render a reproducible survey report
- [`sframe_report_source()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_report_source.md)
  : Recompute and check a report source folder
- [`render_results()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/render_results.md)
  : Render analysis results to a formatted HTML report
- [`sframe_reports`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_reports.md)
  : Choosing a report
- [`sframe_format_result()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_format_result.md)
  : Render one analysis result as the report does
- [`sframe_codebook()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_codebook.md)
  : Generate a survey codebook from an instrument object
- [`sframe_save_figures()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_save_figures.md)
  : Save the charts from an analysis plan as files
- [`sframe_analysis_qmd()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_analysis_qmd.md)
  : Write a Quarto analysis notebook for any instrument
- [`sframe_show()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_show.md) :
  Show a file surveyframe wrote

## References

Cite the works an instrument draws on. The references travel in the
.sframe file and the report lists each one once, at the end. In
SurveyStudio: the References screen. In code:
[`sframe_add_references()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_add_references.md).

- [`sframe_reference()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_reference.md)
  : Create a reference
- [`read_bibtex()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/read_bibtex.md) :
  Read references from BibTeX
- [`sframe_add_references()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_add_references.md)
  : Add references to an instrument
- [`sframe_get_references()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_get_references.md)
  : List an instrument's references
- [`sframe_bibliography()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_bibliography.md)
  : Write a bibliography as CSL-JSON

## Amendments

Change an instrument mid-study, on the record: each amendment is logged
with its reason and the hash it replaced. In SurveyStudio: the
Amendments screen. In code:
[`amend_sframe()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/amend_sframe.md).

- [`amend_sframe()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/amend_sframe.md)
  : Record a disclosed amendment to an instrument
- [`sframe_get_amendments()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_get_amendments.md)
  : Read an instrument's amendment log
- [`sframe_drop_items()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_drop_items.md)
  : Drop items from scales or models
- [`sframe_item_flags()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_item_flags.md)
  : Items past the usual cut-offs in a measurement result
- [`sframe_link_git_commit()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_link_git_commit.md)
  : Link an instrument to its current Git commit

## Inspect

Read parts of an instrument, a validation result or a report without
reaching into the object, at any stage. Each accessor and as.data.frame
method states the classes it accepts and what it returns.

- [`sframe_accessors`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_accessors.md)
  : Explore a surveyframe object
- [`sframe_apa()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_apa.md) :
  Extract APA-formatted result summaries
- [`sframe_get_branches()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_get_branches.md)
  : Get branching rules
- [`sframe_get_attention_checks()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_get_attention_checks.md)
  : Get response-quality checks
- [`sframe_get_choice_sets()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_get_choice_sets.md)
  : Get choice sets
- [`sf_component_list`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sf_component_list.md)
  : A list of instrument components
- [`sframe_flagged()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_flagged.md)
  : Get rows flagged by response-quality checks
- [`sframe_id()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_id.md) : Get
  an instrument component ID
- [`sframe_identity`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_identity.md)
  : The ID and label of an instrument component
- [`sframe_is_valid()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_is_valid.md)
  : Test whether validation passed
- [`sframe_get_items()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_get_items.md)
  : Get survey items
- [`sframe_label()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_label.md)
  : Get an instrument component label
- [`sframe_meta()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_meta.md) :
  Get survey metadata
- [`sframe_missing_columns()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_missing_columns.md)
  : Columns the instrument declares that the responses left out
- [`sframe_get_models()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_get_models.md)
  : Get model specifications
- [`sframe_object()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_object.md)
  : Recover the validated object
- [`sframe_problems()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_problems.md)
  : Get validation problems
- [`sframe_notes()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_notes.md)
  : Notes from a validation
- [`sframe_report_accessors`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_report_accessors.md)
  : Read the reportable parts of an analysis or quality result
- [`sframe_get_scales()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_get_scales.md)
  : Get survey scales
- [`sframe_validation_accessors`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_validation_accessors.md)
  : Read a validation diagnostic
- [`sframe_as_data_frame`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_as_data_frame.md)
  : Coerce a surveyframe object to a data frame
- [`sframe_subset`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_subset.md)
  : Subset a surveyframe report
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sf_choices>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sf_choices.md)
  : Coerce a choice set to a data frame
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe.md)
  : Coerce an instrument to its item summary
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_analysis_results>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_analysis_results.md)
  : Summarise analysis-plan results as a data frame
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_assumption_report>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_assumption_report.md)
  : Coerce an assumption report to a data frame
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_codebook>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_codebook.md)
  : Extract the item table from a codebook report
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_descriptives_report>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_descriptives_report.md)
  : Extract the descriptives results table
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_efa_report>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_efa_report.md)
  : Coerce an EFA readiness report to a data frame
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_efa_solution>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_efa_solution.md)
  : Extract the loading table from an EFA solution
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_item_report>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_item_report.md)
  : Coerce an item report to a data frame
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_missing_data_report>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_missing_data_report.md)
  : Extract item missingness results
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_quality_report>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_quality_report.md)
  : Coerce a response-quality report to a data frame
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_reliability_report>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_reliability_report.md)
  : Coerce a reliability report to a data frame
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_sample_size_plan>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_sample_size_plan.md)
  : Coerce a sample-size plan to a data frame
- [`as.data.frame(`*`<sframe_sensitivity>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/as.data.frame.sframe_sensitivity.md)
  : Extract a sensitivity-analysis results table

## Models and syntax

Declare constructs, paths and covariances, and generate lavaan, seminr
and psych syntax from the instrument.

- [`sframe_model_spec()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_model_spec.md)
  : Create a surveyframe model specification
- [`sframe_construct()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_construct.md)
  : Define a latent or composite construct
- [`sframe_path()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_path.md) :
  Define a structural path between constructs
- [`sframe_covariance()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_covariance.md)
  : Define a covariance between constructs
- [`sframe_indirect_effect()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_indirect_effect.md)
  : Define an indirect effect path
- [`sframe_add_model()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_add_model.md)
  : Add a model specification to an instrument
- [`sframe_validate_model()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_validate_model.md)
  : Validate a surveyframe model specification
- [`sframe_model_json()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_model_json.md)
  : Serialise a model specification to JSON
- [`sframe_model_outline()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_model_outline.md)
  : Create a model reporting template
- [`sframe_syntax_cfa()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_syntax_cfa.md)
  : Generate lavaan CFA syntax from an instrument or a declared model
- [`sframe_syntax_efa()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_syntax_efa.md)
  : Generate EFA planning syntax
- [`sframe_syntax_sem()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_syntax_sem.md)
  : Generate lavaan CB-SEM syntax
- [`sframe_syntax_pls()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_syntax_pls.md)
  : Generate seminr PLS-SEM syntax
- [`sframe_syntax_result()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_syntax_result.md)
  : The R code behind an analysis result

## Charts

Opt-in ggplot2 charts for analysis results, and the package theme.

- [`sframe_plots`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plots.md) :
  Choosing a plot
- [`theme_surveyframe()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/theme_surveyframe.md)
  : surveyframe brand theme for ggplot2
- [`plot(`*`<sframe_analysis_results>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/plot.sframe_analysis_results.md)
  : Plot analysis-plan results
- [`sframe_plot_correlation_matrix()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_correlation_matrix.md)
  : Correlation matrix heatmap
- [`sframe_plot_decision_ranking()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_decision_ranking.md)
  : Ranked-score bar chart for a decision-family result
- [`sframe_plot_dematel_influence()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_dematel_influence.md)
  : Prominence-relation scatter for a DEMATEL result
- [`sframe_plot_descriptives()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_descriptives.md)
  : Distribution shape by variable, standardised
- [`sframe_plot_efa_loadings()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_efa_loadings.md)
  : Loadings heatmap from a fitted EFA solution
- [`sframe_plot_efa_scree()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_efa_scree.md)
  : Scree plot from an EFA readiness report
- [`sframe_plot_group_comparison()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_group_comparison.md)
  : Group-comparison boxplot
- [`sframe_plot_likert_matrix()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_likert_matrix.md)
  : Grouped diverging chart for a Likert matrix question
- [`sframe_plot_likert_scale()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_likert_scale.md)
  : Grouped diverging chart for a scale's Likert items
- [`sframe_plot_missingness()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_missingness.md)
  : Missing-data report plot: missingness rate by item
- [`sframe_plot_paired_comparison()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_paired_comparison.md)
  : Paired-comparison slope plot
- [`sframe_plot_quality()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_quality.md)
  : Quality report plot: straight-lining flag rate by scale
- [`sframe_plot_regression_diagnostics()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_regression_diagnostics.md)
  : Regression diagnostic plots for a regression_linear result
- [`sframe_plot_reliability()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_reliability.md)
  : Reliability plot: alpha and omega by scale
- [`sframe_plot_validity()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_validity.md)
  : Validity report plot: composite reliability and AVE by construct
- [`sframe_plot_variable_distribution()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_variable_distribution.md)
  : Raw-variable distribution panels: histogram, boxplot and Q-Q
- [`sframe_plot_term_frequency()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_term_frequency.md)
  : Term-frequency plot: horizontal bar or word cloud
- [`sframe_plot_ngram_frequency()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_ngram_frequency.md)
  : N-gram-frequency plot: horizontal bar
- [`sframe_plot_cooccurrence()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_cooccurrence.md)
  : Term co-occurrence heatmap
- [`sframe_plot_cooccurrence_network()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_cooccurrence_network.md)
  : Term co-occurrence network plot
- [`sframe_plot_sentiment()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_sentiment.md)
  : Sentiment plot: diverging bar, or a positive/negative comparison
  cloud
- [`sframe_plot_topics()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_plot_topics.md)
  : Topic-model top-terms plot: faceted bars, one facet per topic

## Decision analysis

Multi-criteria decision analysis. The 10 methods run through the
analysis plan like any other, so the functions here assemble their input
and test how stable a ranking is.

- [`sframe_sensitivity_analysis()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_sensitivity_analysis.md)
  : Test how far a decision ranking moves when the weights are perturbed
- [`sframe_assemble_pairwise()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_assemble_pairwise.md)
  : Assemble per-respondent comparison matrices
- [`sframe_aggregate_judgements()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_aggregate_judgements.md)
  : Aggregate individual judgement matrices
- [`sframe_collected_weights()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_collected_weights.md)
  : Criterion weights collected from respondents
- [`sframe_rated_matrix()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_rated_matrix.md)
  : Build a performance matrix from rated matrix items
- [`sframe_decision_options()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_decision_options.md)
  : Normalise the decision options of an analysis-plan block

## Text analysis

Open-ended answers: term and n-gram frequency, keyword in context, and
quote extraction.

- [`sframe_clean_text()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_clean_text.md)
  : Clean open-ended text responses for analysis
- [`sframe_term_frequency()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_term_frequency.md)
  : Term frequency for open-ended text
- [`sframe_ngram_frequency()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_ngram_frequency.md)
  : N-gram frequency for open-ended text
- [`sframe_term_context()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_term_context.md)
  : Keyword-in-context concordance for open-ended text
- [`sframe_extract_quotes()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_extract_quotes.md)
  : Extract representative quotes for each STM topic

## Confidence intervals

Base-R bootstrap and effect-size confidence intervals, reused across the
inferential runners.

- [`sframe_bootstrap_ci()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_bootstrap_ci.md)
  : Percentile bootstrap confidence interval for a statistic
- [`sframe_cohens_d_ci()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_cohens_d_ci.md)
  : Bootstrap confidence interval for Cohen's d
- [`sframe_cramers_v_ci()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_cramers_v_ci.md)
  : Confidence interval for Cramer's V
- [`sframe_eta_sq_ci()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_eta_sq_ci.md)
  : Confidence interval for eta squared

## Demos

25 small teaching demos, each doing one job, and 2 larger reference
datasets. Each comes with an instrument and response data, and the
teaching demos with a codebook and the results surveyframe produced. See
the “Learn by example” article.

- [`sframe_list_demos()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_list_demos.md)
  : List the bundled demos
- [`sframe_demo()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_demo.md) :
  Load one bundled demo
- [`sframe_demo_qmd()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_demo_qmd.md)
  : Copy a demo's Quarto notebook so you can run and change it

## Methods

Print, format and summary methods, so every component prints and
summarises cleanly at the console and inside reports.

- [`print(`*`<sframe>`*`)`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/print.sframe.md)
  : Print an sframe instrument object

## For the report template

The APA cell formatter the Quarto report template calls. Exported
because Quarto renders against the installed package.

- [`sframe_apa_cells()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_apa_cells.md)
  [`sframe_apa_col_labels()`](https://surveyframe.org/reference/sframe_apa_cells.md)
  : Format a result table's cells as an APA 7 report prints them
